BiblicalUsage: massôwr is a saw, and it occurs once, in Isaiah 10:15. There the prophet asks whether the saw shall magnify itself against him that shakes it, as if the rod should shake itself against those who lift it up. The word is the tool that forgets its maker.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe massôwr warns me that the tool does not boast against the workman, and that I am the saw, not the hand.
